steps.content: The next time you hear from Murphy, two weeks have passed.

She tells you she's been waiting for Cranky Old Lady to call these past two weeks, and she never picked up whenever Murphy tried calling. She wouldn't even mind if the woman just showed up in person to chew her out, but that hasn't happened either.
She even broke protocol by accessing the bureau's call records to confirm that none of her colleagues have received any calls from that number either.
And so, in hopes of getting the chance to apologize in person, she drags you onto the streets of Eastside.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But are you sure wandering around aimlessly like this will help you find her? You don't even have her personal information or address, do you?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: The Public Security Bureau's system has an old ID photo she uploaded before... I, uh, took a picture of it. But the address on file is outdated, so we'll just have to search for her ourselves.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: From her previous complaints, I know the general area where she lives. There's a fruit stall downstairs where she always ends up buying rotten persimmons, and a giant billboard on the roof that blocks out all the sunlight in her room... I remember all these details!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So you know the general area, but can you really find the exact location with those vague descriptions?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: That's exactly why I enlisted your help, Chief! Without you, I'd probably just end up getting lost in Eastside!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Let me see... There it is! Look, right over there!

You follow where Murphy's pointing and, miraculously, there it is. A fruit stall piled with overripe persimmons at the corner across the street, and atop the same building stands a massive Quinn billboard.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I knew it! My luck's finally turning around! Let's go, Chief!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait, watch out for the car!
With that confident announcement, Murphy immediately bolts toward the other side of the street. You quickly yank her back, barely avoiding a dump truck turning out from a blind spot.
After that, you grab the unlucky star's arm as you search for a crosswalk, finally arriving at the fruit stall a few minutes later.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Good morning, Rotten Persimmon Lady! Does this old lady in the photo... happen to live in this building?

steps.speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
steps.content: ...What rotten persimmon?! I only sell fresh fruit here!

steps.speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
steps.content: This photo... Oh! That's the old lady who used to live on the second floor. She moved out a couple of days ago. Try looking for her in the neighborhood east of here.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: She... she moved?! Do you... happen to have her address? I really need to reach her. It's important!

steps.speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
steps.content: Why would I have it? Do you even know her, anyway? She never talked to any of the neighbors. We wouldn't have even known she was leaving had we not seen the movers!
The "Rotten Persimmon Lady" looks Murphy and you up and down, apparently deciding if you're some suspicious characters. She then continues.

steps.speaker: Rotten Persimmon Lady
steps.content: If you really want to find her... Look, there's a bus stop over there. Ride four stops. Ask around there with your photo.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Awesome, thank you!
Following the fruit vendor's directions, you and Murphy arrive at the bus stop. Murphy runs her hand over the bus schedule with a wistful and longing expression.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: This brings back memories... You know, Chief, I just realized I haven't taken a bus in ages...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I have a bunch of younger siblings, and the family car couldn't fit everyone, so I always had to take the bus to school.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But there was always something wrong with that bus. Broken AC, a leaking tank, or we'd run into road work... It never made it to the destination without a hitch...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I was always late, and I felt so guilty every time... I brought bad luck to everyone else on the bus. But now you're here with me, so maybe today will be a little luckier.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: We're only riding four stops. What could possibly go wrong?
At that moment, the bus pulls into the station. You and Murphy sit down, but after just two stops, a rear tire suddenly blows out. You're forced to get off the bus along with the other passengers.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Of course... I'm still a hopeless jinx.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...We still have some ground to cover. We can grab two shared bikes here and bike the rest of the way.
You bring Murphy over to a few rental bikes. She crouches down to examine the bright yellow paint, then runs her hand over the handlebars, that same wistful expression crossing her face.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You know, Chief... I just realized I haven't ridden a bike in ages either.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: After I gave up on buses, I saved up and bought myself a beautiful bike. I loved riding it... It made me feel so free and happy. Finally, I didn't have to feel guilty about delaying other people's trips.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But then I accidentally crashed into a pedestrian and sent him into the bushes... I had to sell the bike to cover his medical bills. I haven't ridden a bike ever since...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Okay, stop. Can you please not bring that up right now? I've got a really bad feeling about this.

You and Murphy bike normally for a while, but the peace doesn't last. A few minutes in, you suddenly hear Murphy shout from behind—then a blur shoots past you. It's Murphy, screaming as she barrels downhill completely out of control.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Why won't the brakes work?! Chief!!! HELP!!!

A cacophony of crashing noises echo from the bottom of the slope, followed by a rising cloud of dust. When it settles, you spot an overturned bicycle lodged in the bushes, its rear wheel still spinning in the air.
You grit your teeth and force yourself to stay positive, then pedal down to the bottom of the slope and pull Murphy, sprawled on the ground and covered in leaves, to her feet.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, at least you're not hurt. We've had more than our share of mishaps, but we should be close to our destination now. We can just walk there from here.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You know, Chief...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Don't tell me you haven't walked anywhere in ages either.
Hearing that familiar opening line, you instinctively take two wary steps back.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: No, no! Look, over there! I think we actually made it to our destination!
[Scene Change]
You follow Murphy's gaze. Sure enough, there's a familiar bus stop standing by the roadside, and not far beyond it, a cluster of run-down, low-rise apartment buildings.

You and Murphy park the bicycles by the roadside and start asking around in the residential buildings with the photo. But your luck seems to have run even drier this time. Not a single resident here has ever seen that cranky old lady.

You search from morning through noon and into the afternoon without a single lead. To make matters worse, Murphy somehow gets targeted by someone's dog, and after a relentless chase, the two of you end up cornered in a dead-end alley.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Why does this have to be so hard... I just want to find Cranky Old Lady. We've already made it this far. Why is the home stretch so impossible...
These obviously can't be called coincidences anymore. You sense Murphy's emotions beginning to spiral, her Mania stirring restlessly in response. You quickly reach out to calm her.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Murphy, calm down a little, okay? These are nothing more than some small obstacles. Don't stress yourself out.

steps.speaker: Vicious Dog
steps.content: Woof, woof!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Watch out, it's coming this way again!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ahh! Stay away!!
In a panic, Murphy tears off one of her accessories and hurls it into the distance, hoping to divert the dog's attention.

But as luck would have it, a black cat suddenly leaps down from a tree by the wall and snatches Murphy's accessory from under the dog's nose! The cat flicks its tail smugly, then darts toward a distant corner, jumps over a wall gracefully, and vanishes.
Robbed of its prize, the dog makes to give chase, only to be stopped by its owner's distant shout. With a few reluctant barks, it finally retreats.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...Wait! Did I just... Oh no, that was one of my lucky charms! I need to get it back!

Without hesitation, Murphy rushes over and scrambles up the wall. You follow close behind. The barrier is old and weathered. Through one of the cracks, you lock eyes with someone in the garden behind it.
Who's out there?! How dare you skulk around and steal bricks from my wall?!
Somehow this resident looks familiar to you, but before you can place it, Murphy blurts out.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: There you are! Cranky Old Lady!

steps.speaker: Cranky Old Lady
steps.content: Watch your tongue! Hold on... I know that voice. You're that girl with rotten luck, aren't you? How on earth did you find me here? Even my own son doesn't know where I live.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Um, I didn't find you... A black cat led me here. Whew... Finally! I was so worried something bad had happened to you!
Getting a good look at how disheveled and dust-covered you are, and with the teary-eyed Murphy next to you, the old woman lets out a sigh, suddenly speaking more kindly.

steps.speaker: Cranky Old Lady
steps.content: ...Your unusual luck and your unusual methods. Look at the state of you both. Ran into all sorts of trouble getting here, didn't you? Come on, get down from that wall already. Come sit in the garden.
Murphy agrees cheerfully and positions herself on top of the wall to get ready for the jump. And just as you expect, she lands flat on her face.
[Scene Change]
After you've washed your faces and dressed your wounds, the old lady leads you both into the shabby garden to sit down. She even pours each of you a glass of water.

The property is not only old, but also clearly long-neglected. The wiring and plumbing have fallen into disrepair. The house is poorly furnished. And the plants have been dead for ages. It's obvious it had been abandoned for years, and has only recently regained a resident.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: You shouldn't have come. An old woman like me isn't worth all the trouble you went through.

As she speaks, the old lady explains why she moved here. It turns out she was diagnosed with cancer some time ago. Not wanting to burden her family, she decided to hide away in this abandoned family property where no one could find her.

As for all those complaint calls to the Public Security Bureau, they were a result of her new, lonely life. During that time, lodging complaints gave her some purpose. And Murphy, who listened so patiently, in fact offered her some semblance of companionship.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Never imagined the first person to find me would be you, the girl I used to pester every single day. So how have you been, you poor thing? Still as unlucky as ever?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Oh, you bet! Just look at all these cuts and bruises. Got them when I was searching for you everywhere.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Sigh... You see, I never got much of an education in my life. Didn't make any money when I was young, and now that I'm old, those predatory schemes went and swindled me out of what little I'd saved. I used to wonder, why am I the unlucky one? Everyone else gets to be rich. Why not me?

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Then came all kinds of disasters. My husband passed. I even had to see my own children go... Now I have only one son left. Heh. Turns out I'm the one who outlived them all.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: So many years passed, and I never got rich, but my health held up well enough. And by now... I've actually stopped dwelling on all that.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Why did you stop?

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Because there's no point. I've been unlucky most of my life. Thought I finally got to enjoy some peace in my old age, but here I am, suffering from a terminal illness. How do you make sense of that? You can't. It's just fate.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: So listen, my dear. People with luck like yours and mine must learn to come to terms with life. Whether times are harsh on you or not, life goes on. Whatever it throws at you, try to take it. There's no reasoning with it, but once you make peace with that, you'll find life a lot easier.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But that's... that's not fair at all...
The words leave Murphy visibly shaken. She wants to say something comforting, but can't come up with anything. The old lady notices her struggle and smiles, continuing on.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: You said you came to apologize. Thank you, my dear. But as you see, whatever you said to me is nothing compared to what fate's dealt me. Besides, all you did was give me a bit of attitude. No need to keep blaming yourself.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: You've got nothing to apologize for. Stay a little longer if you like, then go on home and live your life. You've still got plenty of unlucky days ahead of you to get through, okay?
The old woman turns to refill your tea. Murphy lowers her head, lost in thought, processing what she's just heard.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Am I really going to stay unlucky my whole life...? Could... her illness be caused by my bad luck as well...?
Despite everything, she's spiraling once again. A faint trace of Mania begins gathering around her once more. You gently pat her hand, trying to dispel the dark clouds closing in.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Everyone has their own fate. Trust me, your bad luck can't be transferred so easily through a phone line. That much I can guarantee.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Other people's life experiences don't necessarily apply to you. Be curious about them, but you don't have to agree with everything they tell you. That said... "making peace with things" and "not blaming yourself"—those two points I do agree with.
[Scene Change]
You stay with the old lady a while longer before heading back with Murphy. She follows behind you wordlessly, then suddenly stops.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I... I forgot something at the old lady's. I need to go back real quick.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Alright. Hurry back.
With your permission, she turns and jogs back toward the garden.

Just then, you sense a sudden surge of Mania. The Mania field that's been lingering around Murphy like rain clouds suddenly stirs violently and uncontrollably. Through the shackles binding you to her, you feel a tremor run through you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No... Murphy's Mania is flaring up again! Stop, Murphy!
But your voice is quickly drowned out by a deafening explosion...
[Scene Change]
One hour has passed.
Two hours have passed.

You and Murphy sit across from each other in silence, unsure how long you've been waiting outside the emergency room. The nurses passing by all seem uncertain of the situation, refusing to share any concrete details.

On her way back, Murphy stepped on an old, faulty cable in the garden, making it explode. Fortunately, Murphy managed to shield the old lady in that instant, but the woman's frail body could hardly withstand the blast. The garden went ablaze instantly, and now its owner's fate is still unknown inside the emergency room.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I'm so sorry... It's all my fault... If I hadn't gone back, she wouldn't have...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Don't blame yourself for everything. That faulty wiring was an accident waiting to happen. You might have even lessened her injury by protecting her in that moment.
Even so, Murphy remains consumed by guilt. You take her hand, and together you wait for the final outcome.
After what feels like an eternity, the light above the emergency room finally changes color. The door opens, and you seem to be witnessing a miracle.

The old lady you both feared was beyond saving walks out on her own feet, supported by a nurse. Despite her haggard appearance, one arm in a cast and the other clutching two X-ray films, there's an unexpected vitality about her.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Cran... Ma'am! You're okay... I thought you were...
Murphy throws herself into the old lady's arms. Seeing this, the weight that's been pressing on your chest finally vanishes.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Oh goodness... You nearly knocked me over! And stop saying those things that may bring bad luck. I'm fine. I'm not that fragile!

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: You know what, that explosion was actually a blessing in disguise! Sure, it broke my arm, but when the doctors ran their tests, they found out that the cancer diagnosis was a mistake. They'd mixed up my scan with someone else's! Turns out I've been perfectly healthy this whole time!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: The explosion... was a blessing in disguise? How is that even possible? Hold on... The cancer was a misdiagnosis?! That's amazing! You're okay! Does this mean... my bad luck finally turned into good luck?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No... For most people, this would simply mean that there was medical malpractice and the hospital now owes them compensation.

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Oh, you're indeed my lucky star, darling!

steps.speaker: Old Lady
steps.content: Now I don't have to count my remaining days, and I don't have to avoid my own son anymore. Of course, this is no bad luck. It's the greatest blessing I've ever received!
As she speaks with a big smile, tears are streaming down her face at the same time.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well, these two... certainly seem to be on the same wavelength.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Maybe this really is a blessing in disguise after all.
You watch as Murphy and the old lady hold hands, chatting happily for some time. Eventually, the woman's son arrives, and you and Murphy take your leave.
[Scene Change]

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: An explosion and a broken arm certainly sound like a huge disaster to me. But the old lady still called it good luck... And she thought I brought her that blessing?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: After all, whether something is good or bad isn't just about objective facts. There's also the subjective judgment of those who experience it. This event we just went through is simply more dramatic than most.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Whether something is good or bad is subjective... Do I really get to decide... if it's good luck or bad luck?
She looks down at her hands, studying her palms before turning them over to examine the backs, as if contemplating the two sides of a coin—good and bad, fortune and misfortune.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: ...I've learned about so many different things these past few days. Your perspective, the old lady's perspective, the pity system, the aeroplane chess, the black cat, the die...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: The meaning of good luck and bad luck... I think I'm finally starting to get it! For real this time!
You give her a thumbs up in encouragement. She responds with a determined smile.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I need to go home and really think about this. Figure out how to handle the bad things that happen to me, and how to live with these everyday events that have a lucky side and an unlucky side.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief, next time we meet, you'll see a completely transformed Murphy! I promise!
She thumps her chest twice with brimming confidence.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sure, I'm looking forward to it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But it's getting late. Let me take you home. And just to be safe... we'll go on foot.
Her smile suddenly freezes, and her legs tremble slightly at the prospect of the physical ordeal ahead. Meanwhile, you stride forward leisurely as she wails in protest behind you.
